aria: Animated recap of the Nets' 145 to 111 road win at New Orleans: Terance Mann's 3-pointer at the halftime buzzer, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Egor Demin's 22 points in his return, the top scorers, how the Nets won, and Saturday's game at Memphis.
notes: Box score from the Brooklyn Nets' 145–111 road win over the New Orleans Pelicans on Nov 11, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the AP (via CBS Sports), Field Level Media (via The Ticket), the New York Post (Brian Lewis, via Yahoo Sports), the New York Daily News (Fiifi Frimpong, via Yahoo Sports), NetsDaily (Collin Helwig, via Yahoo Sports), Nets Wire and Roundtable Sports (via Yahoo Sports). All 145 Brooklyn points and all 111 New Orleans points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals (83–66 Brooklyn at the half, matching the AP). Team stats are from Covers. Records and the Nets' standing are from the site's standings.

Biggest leads: Brooklyn's 41 and New Orleans' 4 (Covers; the New York Post and Daily News also give 41). Brooklyn's 83 first-half points were its most in a first half since Dec 21, 2022 (AP), and a 17–1 run in the fourth made it 124–84 (AP). Six Nets scored 15 or more, tying a franchise record (New York Post, NetsDaily), and Julius Randle's plus-38 tied Stephon Marbury's franchise record for a road game (New York Post, NetsDaily). Demin returned from a six-game absence (AP, CBS/RotoWire); his 12 fourth-quarter points are from NetsDaily. The win snapped a two-game losing streak (Field Level Media, Nets Wire).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Terance Mann's 3-pointer at the halftime buzzer that capped Brooklyn's 83-point first half and made it 83–66 (New York Daily News, Roundtable Sports; Covers' line score confirms 83–66 at the half). The sources don't say how he got the shot, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Brooklyn Nets or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Mann’s listed 6-foot-6 and 215 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms scaled to his 6-foot-7.75 wingspan at the 2019 draft combine (NBADraft.net), in the Nets' road kit with No. 14 (FOX Sports roster, Wikipedia). He doesn't have an approved look yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
